answers.why: Israel is addressed as God's servant, personifying the nation rather than the patriarch Jacob.
Israel is to be gathered and restored, with the following verse identifying its tribes and survivors.
The preserved of Israel are the people restored alongside the tribes of Jacob.
The LORD is the Redeemer of Israel, the people whose restoration is described immediately before.
The Holy One of Israel names the God of the nation being restored.
The God of Israel protects the departing people addressed with plural pronouns.
The Holy One of Israel is the Redeemer of the community portrayed as a forsaken wife.
The Holy One of Israel is the nation's God, whose glory draws other nations.
Israel has outcasts whom God gathers together with others.
The Holy One of Israel glorifies the community whose children return from afar.
Zion is called the city of the Holy One of Israel, the nation's God.
Israel stands alongside Abraham as an ancestral father who does not acknowledge his descendants.
